identity_notes: Alameda County Superior Court judge. Assigned to RF09456481 in 2010, replacing Judge Thompson without documented reason. Adopted Sala Ajaniku's mediation recommendation without verifying credentials.

CA_Family_Law_Litigator.role: Judge who adopted Ajaniku recommendation without credential verification; reversed protective DVRO; granted Christina unsupervised visitation

US_Federal_Civil_Rights_Litigator.role: §1983 defendant — judicial immunity applies for acts in judicial capacity, but 1996 FRIA amendment (42 USC §1983 as amended) limits injunctive relief immunity; the question is whether adopting a recommendation from an unqualified person is an act 'in judicial capacity' or an administrative failure
US_Federal_Civil_Rights_Litigator.immunity_analysis: Judicial immunity protects judges acting in their judicial capacity even if wrong. However: (1) the 1996 amendment permits injunctive/declaratory relief against judges; (2) if reliance on an unqualified mediator is an administrative rather than judicial act, immunity may not attach; (3) Pulliam v. Allen, 466 U.S. 522 (1984) and its progeny govern the analysis

cross_domain_risk: MEDIUM — protected by judicial immunity for most damages claims, but injunctive relief remains available under the 1996 amendment; the stronger route is naming him for declaratory/injunctive relief while focusing damages claims on the non-immune actors (Ajaniku, Hillberg, Cerretani, APD)
